Later, I noticed that these additives were billed separately on a different invoice, while the actual servicing bill was a genuine Royal Enfield service bill. This practice is misleading, as customers may assume everything is part of the official service.
Additionally, I was advised to take an AMC for discounts and offers, which I accepted. The AMC was valid for one year. After the AMC expired, when a part still under company warranty was damaged, the service center informed me that warranty claims would be processed only if I take AMC again.
Instead of honoring the warranty, they mentioned they were replacing the part as a “goodwill”, which is not correct. Warranty should not be linked to AMC, as AMC is optional and warranty is a customer right.
Sales experience was good, but after-sales service, billing transparency, and warranty handling are disappointing. Customers should be clearly informed about optional add-ons and warranty terms.
